title: HIRES error gains from early 28-day GJ 667C templates differ between two HARPS reductions
abstract: We test whether 45 public HIRES exposures support early 28-day GJ 667C templates from two HARPS reductions. We average conditional period-profile templates from 182 early HARPS exposures. With 2 m/s extra noise, the DRS template reduces HIRES squared error by 7.75 percent with all exposures and 15.82 percent after a photon cut. The SERVAL template gives -0.20 and +2.87 percent. Trends, a detector step and a 7-day wave are fitted again in HIRES. An S-index term and 4 m/s extra noise retain the pattern in point gains. Conditional Gaussian power at a 1 percent threshold is below 48 percent, and observed scatter exceeds the 2 m/s noise model. Different mean templates, overlapping scale intervals, period bounds and stellar noise limit inference. Some HIRES data were used in prior planet reports. This is a separate-instrument check of a known signal, not a new planet or a new observing campaign. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval steps are supplied. External observation records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Early HARPS period loss profiles and formal HIRES template scale intervals. The intervals assume independent Gaussian errors and omit template uncertainty.

citations.reason: Supplies the broad-line guard and unresolved 28-day control.
Shows period uncertainty can cause a failed early forecast. We add a separate instrument and mean profile template test.
